events_chronological: As a young man scavenging in the closed city of Vyrsk, Yuri Sarkin finds a buried cache of gold and a message from the future, and is hired to assemble the Device.
In the future, the scientist who built the Device splits it into nine pieces, hides them in the past, and kills herself so that it cannot be rebuilt.
Dying of cancer, Sarkin decides to take the world with him by assembling the Device and reversing entropy.
An intelligence operative survives a siege at a concert hall and swallows a cyanide pill that turns out to be a loyalty test, and is recruited into the organisation.
The operative is shown inverted bullets and briefed by a scientist on objects whose entropy runs backwards.
He traces the bullets to the arms dealer Devi, who names Sarkin as the source.
An official called Ballard tells him to reach Sarkin through his estranged wife Ana, an art appraiser trapped by a forged painting she authenticated.
The operative and Vidal break into the airport freeport to steal the forgery and are attacked by a masked man moving backwards through the fight.
Ana introduces the operative to Sarkin, who tries to have him killed on the yacht.
Sarkin takes the operative along on a raid to seize a radioactive core from a motorway convoy in the coastal city.
The operative hides the case, Sarkin shoots Ana with an inverted bullet, and the operative gives up the case to save her.
The operative and Vidal invert themselves and drive the convoy chase backwards to recover the case, and the operative fights the masked man in the freeport - himself.
The inverted Ana is taken back through the freeport turnstile to be healed before the radiation kills her.
The team work out that Sarkin's dead-man switch will detonate the Device at the moment of his death, on a yacht off a southern coast days earlier.
A temporal pincer movement is mounted at Vyrsk, with one team moving forward and one backward through the same ten minutes.
On the yacht, Ana keeps Sarkin alive until the signal comes, and then kills him herself.
In the hypocentre, the operative and a soldier reach the Device, and a corpse with a red-tagged rucksack opens the gate for them.
Vidal reveals that he was that corpse, that he has known the operative for years from the other direction, and goes back to die.
The operative kills Devi to protect Ana and her son, and understands that he is himself the founder of the organisation who recruited them all.
nonlinear_category_reason: The mission holds 13 of 16 scenes and runs forward, with the antagonist's youth and the future scientist arriving as earlier exposition.
syuzhet_notes: The film follows the operative's personal timeline, which runs forward, but from told-order bullet 12 that timeline is running backwards through world time - the convoy chase and the freeport fight of told-order bullets 6 and 9 are replayed from the other direction, so the audience watches the same events a second time with causes and effects swapped. Told-order bullets 4, 8 and 11 are exposition reaching decades back or centuries forward.
fabula_notes: World chronology and personal chronology diverge for most of the second half, and several characters are present in the same room twice moving in opposite directions, so any single ordering has to pick one clock; this one follows world time. The partner's whole acquaintance with the operative runs opposite to the operative's and is never shown, only stated in his last scene.
